claims.short_name: Unique large maximum-degree obstruction up to 2D+1 vertices
claims.claim_text: If a finite simple graph has maximum degree at most D=alpha+beta, positive caps and at most 2D+1 degree-D vertices, an alpha/beta-capped edge split fails iff both caps are odd and there is an isolated connected odd-order D-regular component.
claims.support_summary: General paper proof from the ordinary Lovasz tight-component parity factor criterion; all small counted components pay at least D weighted boundary, so with one large component it must have zero boundary and be isolated. Independent C++17 verification 91,657 capped instances below the threshold.

claims.short_name: 264 new ordered three-star exclusions; all forced degrees >=5 covered conditionally
claims.claim_text: Assuming the current paper-level joint three-star residual theorem, unique-large-core classification and three explicit exterior-colouring constructions exclude 264 additional ordered 3x3 parameter pairs beyond the prior 339-case method shortlist, leaving 75 survivors, all with forced degree at most 4. Combined with the earlier analytic large-degree theorem, the original conjectured formula holds conditionally for all 3-star pairs with both leading sizes >=2 and their sum >=7.
claims.support_summary: Two fresh independent whole-domain exact Python enumerations agree on all 264 exclusions and 75 survivors: 176 parity, 10 leaf-edge exterior, 63 core/exterior monochrome, and 15 minimal exterior recolouring. The paper theorem is explicitly conditional on the earlier joint three-star residual proof; no unrestricted conjecture solution.
